Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:10:1.hebrew: לימא שמואל - דאקפיד, כיחידאה סבירא ליה, כההיא מתניתא: במחובר, אפי' כולו אבוד נמי אסור, ואוקימנא כר' יוסי יחידאה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:10:1.english: Shall we say that Shmuel - who took offense, holds in accordance with the individual [opinion], like that Baraita: [Regarding produce] that is still attached [to the ground], even if all of it would be lost, it is also forbidden [to harvest it], and we established it [as following] Rabbi Yosei, who is an individual [opinion]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:10:2.hebrew: חצדא דחיטי דלא הוה פסידא - להכי איקפד, אבל בחצדא דשערי לא סבר לה כר' יוסי דאסיר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:10:2.english: It was a harvest of wheat, which would not have been lost - For this reason [Shmuel] was angered; but regarding a harvest of barley, he does not hold like Rabbi Yose, who prohibits [it]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:11:1.hebrew: אין לו מה יאכל הוה - רב, להכי עביד הכי:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:11:1.english: He had nothing to eat - [Rav]; therefore he did this:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:11:2.hebrew: לא סיימוה קמיה - לא אמרו לו לשמואל דלא הוה ליה לרב מה יאכל, להכי איקפד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:11:2.english: They did not complete it before him - They did not tell him [Shmuel] that [Rav] did not have anything to eat; therefore [Shmuel] became angry.

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:11:3.hebrew: אדם חשוב שאני - רב לא הוה ליה למיעבד הכי, אפי' אין לו מה יאכל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:11:3.english: An important person is different - Rav should not have acted this way, even though he had nothing to eat:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:12:1.hebrew: נפק - רבי יהודה נשיאה בחצר בשבת:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:12:1.english: He went out - [Rabbi Yehuda Nesia went out] into the courtyard on Shabbat:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:12:2.hebrew: בחומרתא דמדושא - טבעת היא של מתכת, וחותמה של אלמוג:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:12:2.english: With a chumarta of Medusha - It is a metal ring, and its seal is of coral:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:13:1.hebrew: כל שהוא נאכל כמות שהוא חי - ומיא שתו אינשי כמות שהן:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:13:1.english: Anything that is eaten as it is raw - and people drink water as it is [raw]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:13:2.hebrew: אדם חשוב שאני - יש לו להחמיר על עצמו יותר, ולא הוה ליה למיפק בחומרתא דמדושא, ולא למישתי מיא דאחים קפילא נכרי:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:13:2.english: An important person is different - He should be more stringent with himself, and he should not have gone out [wearing] the cloak [lit. stringency] of Medusha, nor drunk water that a gentile cook [kapeila] had heated:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:14:1.hebrew: לנסורת - עצים דקים שנופלין מן החתיכה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:14:1.english: For its sawdust - the fine pieces of wood that fall from the cut [piece]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:15:2.hebrew: בשלנייא - פירוש, שם העיר; כלומר, היה לו יער באותו מקום:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:15:2.english: In Shelaniya - This is the name of a city; that is, he had a forest in that place:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:15:3.hebrew: אישתמיט נרגא בעי למיפסקיה לשקיה - דרב אשי, משום דעבר אדאביי:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:15:3.english: The ax slipped; it was about to cut off his leg - [This was the ax] of Rav Ashi, because he transgressed [the words of] Abaye:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:15:4.hebrew: שבקיה - לאבא, דלא קצציה במועד, שהרגיש משום דעבר אדאביי, נפל ליה נרגא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:15:4.english: He left it - [He left] the forest, and did not cut it down during the Festival [intermediate days], because he sensed that he had transgressed [the ruling of] Abaye. The ax fell from him:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:16:1.english: To uproot flax - on the intermediate days of the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:16:3.english: Keshuta - [This is] hops (homlon in Old French):

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:16:4.hebrew: לחפיפה - לכסות בו מאכל, כגון תאנים ותמרים, לצורך המועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:16:4.english: For a cover [ḥafifa] - to cover food with it, such as figs and dates, for the needs of the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:16:5.hebrew: לנזיי - כמו דאמרינן נזייתא דשיכרא (ב"ק דף לה.): לנזיי, גרעינין דאית בהו בשומשמין, דחזו למיעבד בהו משחא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:16:5.english: For the nazyei - Like [the expression] "the nazyata of beer" (Bava Kamma 35a): "For the nazyei" means the seeds that are in the sesame plants, which are suitable for making oil from them:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:17:1.hebrew: אפקריה ר' ינאי לפרדיסיה - משום דעל ידו היה תקלה לעלמא, דשהו עד לחולא דמועדא וקטפי:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:17:1.english: Rabbi Yannai declared his orchard ownerless - because through him there was a stumbling block for the world, as [others] delayed [their harvests] until the intermediate days of the Festival and harvested [then]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:18:2.hebrew: שלא יכוין מלאכתו במועד - שיש לו פנאי בשאר ימות השנה, והוא משהה את מלאכתו למועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:18:2.english: That he not plan his work for the Festival - [That is, that] he has free time during the rest of the days of the year, and he delays [his work] until the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:18:3.english: Must be lost - for it is forbidden to derive benefit from them:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:1:1.hebrew: יש מהן פטור אבל אסור - והא דקתני "אין זופתין", אסור למיעבד לכתחילה, אבל בדיעבד לא הוי חייב; והא דקתני "זופתין", הוי מותר לכתחילה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:1:1.english: Some of them are exempt but prohibited - And that which [the Mishnah] taught, "one may not caulk," [means that] it is prohibited to do so ab initio, but after the fact one is not liable; and that which it taught, "one may caulk," [means that] it is permitted ab initio:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:21:1.hebrew: צינעא דידיהו יממא הוא - אפי' בלילה כיממא דמי, ולא סגי ליה שלא להכניסן, להכי מכניסן נמי ביום:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:21:1.english: The discretion of these is the daytime - Even at night it is like daytime [in terms of concealment], and it is not possible for him not to bring them in; therefore he brings them in during the day as well.

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:22:1.hebrew: מהו שיקנסו בניו אחריו - לבניו נמי יהא אסור אותה מלאכה? דכיון דכוון מלאכתו במועד, דין הוא שיהו אסורין ליהנות ממנה, כשם שהיה אביהם קיים:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:22:1.english: What is [the halakha] — should his sons be penalized after him? - Should that product of labor be forbidden to his sons as well? For since he intended [to do] his labor on the Festival [intermediate days], it is logical that they should be forbidden to benefit from it, just as [it would have been] had their father been alive:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:2:1.hebrew: למיחצד - לקצור. ורב הונא יש לו מה יאכל הוה, ואמאי שרי לה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:2:1.english: To harvest - To reap. But Rav Huna had what to eat, so why was it permitted for him?

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:4:1.hebrew: אמר ליה - האי דקתני: מחובר אפי' כולו אבוד, נמי אסור — ר' יוסי היא, ויחידאה היא, ולא סבירא לן כוותיה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:4:1.english: He said to him - This [ruling] that it teaches, that attached [produce], even if all of it is lost, is also prohibited, is [the view of] Rabbi Yosei, and it is an individual opinion, and we do not hold in accordance with it:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:6:1.hebrew: כיון דכל יומא לאו בפרות דיישי האידנא לאו שינוי הוא - כי דיישי בלא פרות, ולעולם הדין כדעת ר' יוסי היא, והא דאסר בפרות, משום דאוושא מילתא היא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:6:1.english: Since every day one does not thresh with cows, now too it is not a change - When they thresh without cows, [it is permitted]; and in truth, [the ruling] is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, and [the reason] that he prohibited [threshing] with cows is because it would make the matter publicly noticeable:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:7:1.hebrew: ואם טחן - במועד לצורך המועד, והותיר עד לאחר המועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:7:1.english: And if he ground - on the Festival [intermediate days] for the sake of the Festival, and [some] was left over until after the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:7:2.english: It is permitted - to eat it after the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:8:1.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יערים - שלא יעשה הרבה, ויאמר: לצורך המועד אני עושה, ומתכוין כדי שתשתייר לאחר המועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:8:1.english: Provided that he does not employ an artifice - [meaning] that he should not make a large quantity and say, "I am making it for the need of the Festival," while intending that some will be left over after the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:9:1.hebrew: מערים ושותה מן החדש - שיכול לומר: לצורך המועד הטילו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 12b:9:1.english: He may employ an artifice and drink from the new - for he can say, "I brewed it for the sake of the Festival."

Tosafot on Moed Katan 12b:18:1.hebrew: מכניס אדם פירותיו מפני הגנבים - פירש בתוספות של הרב, דבאסיפת פירות איכא מלאכה, כדאמרינן פרק אין דורשין (חגיגה דף יח.) גבי חג האסיף: אסיפה במועד מי שרי? ואיני יודע מה מלאכה, וצריך עיון אי טרח בלא מלאכה אסיר, כי היכי דאסירי בפרקמטיא. ולקמן בשמעתין (מועד קטן דף יג) אמר: מועד משום טירחא, ולא טירחא הוא. ושמא היינו דוקא בדבר שהוא מלאכה:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 12b:18:1.english: A person may bring in his fruit because of thieves - The Rav explained in the Tosafot that in the gathering of fruit there is [forbidden] labor, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Ein Dorshin (Chagigah 18a) regarding the Festival of Ingathering: "Is gathering permitted on the intermediate days of the Festival?" But I do not know what labor [is involved], and it requires further study whether exertion without [actual] labor is forbidden, just as [exertion] is forbidden in trade. And later in our passage (Moed Katan 13) it says: "The intermediate days of the Festival [were established] for the sake of exertion [i.e., rest], and this is not exertion." Perhaps this applies specifically to a matter that is [actual] labor:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 12b:23:1.hebrew: אם תימצי לומר צרם אזן הבכור ומת קנסו בנו אחריו - משום דאיסורא עשה, אבל כוון מלאכתו לא עשה איסורא עדיין, ולא צריך להגיה דאורייי'. אבל בפ' השולח (גיטין מד. ושם), דגבי מכר ומת בעי אי קנסו בנו אחריו, התם גרסינן ודאי איסורא דאורייתא, משום דמכר ומת נמי עבד איסור', אלא דלא הוי דאוריי':
Tosafot on Moed Katan 12b:23:1.english: If you might say that [if one] nicked the ear of a firstborn [animal] and it died, we penalize his son after him - because he did a prohibited act, but one who [merely] directed his work [toward a permitted purpose] had not yet committed a prohibition, and it is not necessary to amend [the text to read] "Torah [prohibition]." But in the chapter Hashole'ach (Gittin 44a, and there), where regarding [one who] sold [a slave] and died, [the Gemara] asks whether we penalize his son after him — there we certainly read "a Torah prohibition," because [one who] sold and died also committed a prohibition, except that it was not a Torah [prohibition]:
